🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/operator/starter.go (1)
`227-235`: _📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _💤 Low value_ **Regex matcher for a single exact condition type.** Using `regexp.MustCompile("^NodeControllerDegraded$")` for an exact-string match works correctly but adds unnecessary regex overhead/complexity for a single literal comparison. This same tradeoff was raised in a similar `cluster-etcd-operator` PR using the identical `status.MustNewInertia` pattern, where a reviewer suggested library-go could support exact matching to avoid the regex call, though it was called "not blocking at all." Given the current library-go API only supports `ConditionTypeMatcher *regexp.Regexp`, this is the correct idiomatic usage today — flagging only as an optional readability nit, not a functional issue.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/operator/starter.go` around lines 227 - 235, The exact match in newDegradedInertia currently uses regexp.MustCompile for a single literal condition type, which is unnecessary complexity for a one-value comparison. If library-go has an exact-match helper or can be extended in status.MustNewInertia/ConditionTypeMatcher to support string equality, switch newDegradedInertia to that API; otherwise leave the existing regexp as-is since it is the only supported option today. ```
